title: quick accent inserts `」` as `「` in the wechat desktop app
author: brauljo
summary: Quick Accent reportedly produces U+300C instead of U+300D in WeChat. The mapping contains both characters and uses Unicode SendInput, but the report does not prove whether selection, handoff, WeChat, or an active IME changes the character.

status.label: Controlled reproduction needed
status.detail: A WeChat, Notepad, and clipboard-paste comparison is needed before selecting a compatibility implementation.

next_action.label: Reproduce CJK punctuation insertion
next_action.reason: Confirm the selected code point and isolate a PowerToys selection defect from target-specific synthetic-input handling.

judgment.rationale: The report provides a precise expected/actual character pair and target application, so a maintainer can reproduce it. The evidence does not distinguish an adjacent-character selection or handoff problem from WeChat or IME transformation of Unicode synthetic input.
evidence: The issue reports that intended U+300D `」` becomes U+300C `「` in WeChat Desktop.
The attached diagnostic confirms Quick Accent was enabled on PowerToys 0.100.2, with Pinyin enabled and usage sorting configured.
CharacterMappings.cs contains distinct U+300C and U+300D Pinyin entries.
PowerAccent sends the selected character through WindowsFunctions.Insert, which uses SendInput with KEYEVENTF_UNICODE.
The diagnostic and current Quick Accent logs do not record the picker selection or emitted Unicode code point.
Issue 44848 separately reports incorrect Quick Accent selection, so selection/handoff remains a credible alternative explanation.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the controlled current-version reproduction and request only the WeChat, IME, picker, neutral-target, and paste evidence that differentiates the candidate causes.

fix_assessment.rationale: No PowerToys fix attempt covers this report. A conditional compatibility direction is plausible, but must not be approved until controlled reproduction proves that Quick Accent emits U+300D and only the target path changes it.

proposed_fixes.title: Evaluate an opt-in clipboard insertion strategy for incompatible targets
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed hypothesis: WeChat or the active IME changes the VK_PACKET/WM_CHAR sequence generated by Quick Accent after Quick Accent selects U+300D. An adjacent-character selection or handoff defect is not yet excluded.
plan: Reproduce with the picker visibly identifying U+300D, then compare the identical commit in Notepad, WeChat, and normal clipboard paste.
If Quick Accent emits U+300D and only WeChat changes it, instrument the commit path in PowerAccent.SendInputAndHideToolbar and WindowsFunctions.Insert to preserve that evidence.
Only then design an explicitly configured application-list fallback that retains Unicode SendInput by default and selects clipboard paste for confirmed incompatible applications.
Prepare clipboard data successfully before deleting the base character, bound clipboard-contention retries, and clean up partial Ctrl+V input so a failure cannot lose text or leave modifiers pressed.
verification: Test U+300C, U+300D, U+300E, and U+300F in current WeChat and Notepad using the same keyboard layout and IME mode.
Confirm that the default Unicode path preserves the clipboard and that an opt-in fallback inserts the chosen code point without deleting text on clipboard or SendInput failure.
Exercise clipboard contention, focus changes, elevated targets, surrogate pairs, and partial input delivery.

confidence.rationale: The target-specific synthetic-input hypothesis matches the code path and analogous public WeChat evidence, but this report has no neutral-target comparison or event evidence and does not prove the selected code point.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent reportedly changes a selected closing corner bracket into an opening corner bracket only in WeChat Desktop.
known_information: The affected PowerToys version is 0.100.2 and the diagnostic archive is already attached.
Quick Accent is enabled with the Pinyin character set and usage sorting.
The source mapping contains distinct entries for U+300C and U+300D.
Quick Accent commits selected text through Unicode SendInput.
There are no comments, assignees, linked PRs, or a matching PowerToys fix attempt.
inferences: WeChat or the active IME may transform Unicode synthetic input, but that is not confirmed for this report.
A mapping typo is less likely because U+300D is present in the mapping, while selection of the adjacent entry remains unexcluded.
Clipboard paste may be a compatibility fallback, but a universal fallback would impose clipboard and UX risks.
issue_context.analysis: The evidence narrows the uncertainty to selection/handoff versus target delivery. A controlled U+300D picker capture, neutral-target comparison, and paste comparison will distinguish those paths without requesting a duplicate diagnostic archive.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, labels, attachment, and timeline.
Inspected CharacterMappings.cs, PowerAccent.SendInputAndHideToolbar, WindowsFunctions.Insert, and relevant Quick Accent tests.
Reviewed current Quick Accent input-path changes and Issue 44848.
Reviewed analogous public WeChat reports involving KEYEVENTF_UNICODE as supporting, not conclusive, evidence.

reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys release; repeat on 0.100.2 only for comparison if necessary.
prerequisites: Quick Accent enabled with the Pinyin set
setup: Preserve the reporter's configuration first, then repeat with Pinyin only and usage sorting disabled.
steps: Focus a WeChat message field and use Quick Accent to highlight U+300D `」` in the picker.
Commit the selection and record the resulting character.
Repeat the identical selection in Notepad under the same keyboard layout and IME mode.
Paste the literal `」` into the same WeChat field and compare the result.
Repeat for U+300C, U+300E, and U+300F.
reproduce.expected_result: Each explicitly selected or pasted code point remains unchanged.

actions.label: Request current target comparison

comment.body: Thanks for the report and the attached diagnostic archive. It confirms that Quick Accent was enabled, but it does not show whether the picker selected U+300D or whether the change happens only in WeChat. Could you retest on the current PowerToys release and share: (1) the exact WeChat version/install channel and active Windows input method or punctuation mode; (2) a short recording or screenshots showing Quick Accent's Unicode description for U+300D followed by the result in both WeChat and Notepad; and (3) whether pasting the literal `」` into that same WeChat field keeps it unchanged? No additional bug-report ZIP is needed unless the behavior changes.
